description:
FILED s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), found probing #571.  Tiny and almost
certainly unreachable in real code, but it is a silent VALUE divergence.

REPRO:
    for my $v (0, 1, 2, 5, -3, "x", "") { $^C = $v; print "set=[$v] got=[$^C]\n" }
  perl: 0 1 1 1 1 0 0
  PCL:  0 1 2 5 -3 x ""

perl's $^C is PL_minus_c, a C flag, and its magic set is (bool)SvIV(sv) -- so
the stored value is the NUMIFIED value's truth, which is why "x" (numifies to
0) stores 0 while -3 stores 1.  PCL (task #571) gives it an ordinary
`(defvar |$^C| (make-p-box 0))`, which stores whatever it is handed.

The same question applies to the other flag-shaped caret cells that PCL keeps
as plain boxes -- $^D, $^F, $^P, $^W -- and each has its own perl coercion
($^W is also a bool, $^F an int).  Measure them together before writing code.

WHY IT IS FILED AND NOT FIXED: PCL never sets $^C itself (no -c mode) and a
program assigning anything but 0/1 to it is doing nothing meaningful.  The fix
needs a p-magic-cell (a getter/setter pair) on the box, which puts an
indirection on every READ of the variable for a value nobody reads -- so it
should only be done if it can be done as a shared "flag-shaped caret cell"
mechanism for the whole family, not as a one-off.

BAR: the seven-value probe above for each name in the family, vs perl; a row in
Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t; cl/ change so the merge review's sweep covers it.
subject: assignment to $^C is a BOOL in perl ((bool)SvIV) and a plain store in PCL: $^C = 5 reads 5, perl reads 1
